title: Character IR - shared definitions
description: Building blocks used by every layer of the character IR: identifiers and typed references, evidence and confidence, index spaces, engine addresses, quantities, encodings, and the per-engine extension slot that lets Melee (m-ex / GD's Melee port) and Brawl (BrawlEx / PSA) data live side by side in one engine-neutral document.

Id.description: A document-local identifier: '<namespace>:<path>'. The namespace names the entity kind (e.g. 'joint', 'motion', 'state', 'script', 'tex', 'file', 'fn', 'slot'); the path is free-form but stable within the document. Every entity that anything else may point at carries an 'id'.

Ref.description: A reference to an entity in this document (an Id), or in another IR document ('<document id>#<Id>'), e.g. another fighter that this one clones.

Confidence.description: How much a fact can be trusted. verified: parsed and cross-checked against a second source (another file, a run, a log). observed: seen at runtime/in a log but not cross-checked. inferred: read from code or structure, not run. assumed: a working assumption (say why in a note). unknown: not determined (the value, if any, is a placeholder).

EvidenceRef.description: Id of an entry in the document's evidence registry ('ev:<name>').

Evidence.description: One source a fact rests on. Kept in a registry at the document root and referenced by id, so a single tool run or file offset can back many facts.

path.description: File path (relative to the repo root where possible) or URL.

lines.description: Line range for source evidence, e.g. '1336-1351'.

revision.description: Commit / build / disc revision the evidence was taken from.

command.description: Tool invocation that produced the evidence.

Provenance.description: Attach to any object: how sure we are and why. Omitted = inherit from the enclosing object.

Hex.description: An integer written as hex ('0x...'); used for addresses, offsets, flags and ids where the hex form is the one people search for.

EngineId.description: An engine/runtime a fact is specific to. 'melee.gc' = retail SSBM (GALE01 v1.02) on GameCube hardware; 'melee.mex' = the m-ex framework's semantics; 'melee.gdport' = GD's Melee PC port; 'brawl.wii' = retail SSBB (RSBE01); 'brawl.brawlex' = BrawlEx / P+Ex style fighter expansion; 'brawl.psa' = the Project Smash Attacks move-set format. New engines use the same dotted form.

EngineExtensions.description: Engine-specific detail that has no engine-neutral meaning. Keys are EngineIds; values are free-form objects whose shape is documented per engine in schema/engines/*.md. Semantic fields stay outside this block so that two engines' versions of the same concept can be compared field by field.

IndexSpace.description: A named numbering. The IR never stores a bare index: it says which space the number is in, because the same fighter is 56 in one space and 61 in another (Shadow: m-ex internal 56, m-ex external 55, port slot 28, port FighterKind 61, port CharacterKind 62).

space.description: Dotted space name. Known spaces: melee.retail.character_kind, melee.retail.fighter_kind, melee.mex.internal, melee.mex.external, melee.mex.css_icon, melee.gdport.mex_slot, melee.gdport.fighter_kind, melee.gdport.character_kind, melee.item_kind, melee.effect_bank, melee.ssm_bank, melee.sfx_id, melee.gfx_id, melee.motion_id, melee.stage.external, melee.stage.internal, brawl.fighter_id, brawl.slot_id, brawl.css_slot_id, brawl.cosmetic_id, brawl.soundbank_id, brawl.action_id, brawl.subaction_id, brawl.article_id, brawl.effect_bank.

stability.description: stable: fixed by the content. install_relative: depends on what else is installed/enabled (the port's dense m-ex slots shift when a mod is disabled). session_relative: assigned at run time.

IndexMapping.description: An explicit function between two index spaces, with its rule and where it is implemented.

partial.description: True when some inputs have no image (e.g. an external id the port has no slot for returns -1).

CodeLocation.description: A place in a code base (decomp, port, framework asm, tool).

EngineAddress.description: An address in an engine's own address space (e.g. a GameCube retail function 0x800693AC), kept symbolic so it can be re-targeted: the IR never assumes the address is callable as-is on another host.

unit.description: Owning translation unit, needed to tell same-named statics apart.

base_symbol.description: For data_interior: the object the address points into.

host_binding.description: How a host runtime resolves it (e.g. GD's Melee: bridged native gw_<symbol>, redirected static, API shim).

CallSignature.description: Argument/return classes of a callable as the calling convention sees them. Engine-neutral classes; the ABI mapping (PPC EABI GPR/FPR, x86 cdecl, ...) is given by 'abi'.

variadic_rule.description: How variadic floats are detected (PPC: CR6 bit set before the call; printf-style: from the format string).

quirks.description: Call-site ABI quirks content relies on, e.g. a callee reading a register the caller never set (it_80276174 reads r4).

ValueClass.description: i32/u32: integer register; ptr: pointer (address space in 'space'); f32/f64: float register; void; agg:<size>: by-value aggregate of <size> bytes.

AddressSpace.description: Where a pointer points. guest.mem1 = emulated GameCube main RAM (big-endian, snapshotted); guest.aram = audio RAM; engine.static = a retail static whose bytes the port keeps in native .data at the retail address; host.stack / host.heap = native memory; guest.persist = the port's never-freed m-ex region; mmio = hardware registers (e.g. the GX write-gather pipe); file = offset inside a file.

Quantity.description: A number with a unit. Game-space distances are in the engine's units (Melee/Brawl: 1 unit ~ 1 'stage unit').

raw.description: The stored value before unit conversion (e.g. fixed-point), when it differs.

Encoding.description: How a value or stream is stored, so a writer can reproduce it byte-exactly. Semantic fields hold the decoded value; this records the storage.

BlobRef.description: Bulk data kept out of the JSON (vertex buffers, decoded keyframes, pixels, disassembly). Points at a sidecar file next to the IR document, or at a byte range in a source file.

Issue.description: A defect, gap or risk found while building the IR - in the content, the framework, or the host runtime.
